summary: Mortal Kombat entries from Sami's spine and sourced supplemental seeds, built for per-platform route research.

entries.title: Mortal Kombat (2011)

sami.notes: ps3 exclusive and ps voita exclusive content

entries.definitive_edition: PC Komplete Edition plus PS3/Vita exclusive-content pass

emulation.emulator: Native PC; RPCS3/Vita3K optional for secondary validation
emulation.notes: Use native PC for the main run. Use original PlayStation hardware or carefully validated emulation only for PlayStation-exclusive sampling.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: PC Komplete Edition plus PS-exclusive samples

primary.version: Mortal Kombat: Komplete Edition on PC
primary.why: Sami selected PC, and the Windows Komplete Edition contains the main DLC package with the highest capture/settings ceiling. PlayStation-only content still needs a secondary pass because Kratos is PlayStation-exclusive and the Vita version adds its own costumes, Challenge Tower, touch features, and Tremor challenge appearances while removing one stage.
primary.how_to_play: Play Mortal Kombat: Komplete Edition on Windows if already owned or available from a legitimate copy; then sample PlayStation 3/Vita exclusive content separately.

secondary.exclusive_content: Kratos as a PlayStation-exclusive fighter and PlayStation-only 3D display mode.
secondary.what_to_play: Sample Kratos-specific ladder/versus content after the PC Komplete Edition run.
secondary.why: Kratos is a PlayStation exclusive, and the PS3 version has an exclusive 3D display mode.

secondary.exclusive_content: Vita-only costumes, new Challenge Tower, touchscreen features, and Tremor appearances in character challenge towers, with one stage removed.
secondary.what_to_play: Play the Vita Challenge Tower/exclusive-costume content only; do not repeat the whole story run.
secondary.why: The Vita version has additions and a removed stage.

entries.remaster_caveats: The Windows Komplete Edition was removed from Steam in 2020; use an already-owned legitimate copy or console Komplete Edition if PC access is unavailable.

entries.title: Mortal Kombat (1992)

emulation.emulator: MAME-style arcade emulation optional
emulation.notes: Original arcade hardware is the reference; accurate arcade emulation is acceptable if the revision is verified.

primary.why: Sami selected the arcade release and noted the Rev 5.0 T-Unit target. Arcade is the original and best-fidelity reference; later home ports and compilations are access routes with compromises or modern-wrapper caveats.
primary.how_to_play: Use an original arcade board or an accurate arcade-emulation setup targeting the selected revision; use Legacy Kollection/Arcade Kollection only as a convenience route after checking latency and revision behavior.

entries.remaster_caveats: The exact Sami revision is preserved as a target; public sources used here support the arcade route but not the revision details, so confidence is medium.

entries.title: Mortal Kombat Mythologies Sub-Zero

emulation.emulator: DuckStation optional
emulation.notes: Original PlayStation hardware or PS1 emulation is appropriate; verify FMV playback timing.

primary.why: Sami selected PlayStation; the PlayStation version is superior because the Nintendo 64 port stripped out the FMV cutscenes and had lower-quality audio.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PlayStation disc on original PS1/PS2 hardware or a PS1 emulator; use Legacy Kollection only as a modern convenience route after checking preservation accuracy.

entries.remaster_caveats: No standalone remaster is documented; Legacy Kollection is a compilation wrapper.

entries.title: Mortal Kombat Gold

emulation.emulator: Flycast or Redream optional
emulation.notes: Original Dreamcast hardware is the reference; Dreamcast emulation is a practical capture route.

primary.version: Original Dreamcast release, revised disc preferred if available
primary.why: Sami selected Dreamcast, and Mortal Kombat Gold was a Dreamcast-only updated version of Mortal Kombat 4 with extra characters and stages. Because the first release had major bugs, use the revised disc where possible.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Dreamcast disc on Dreamcast hardware or Flycast/Redream; prefer the revised disc if you can verify it.

entries.remaster_caveats: The launch version had serious bugs/glitches; use a revised disc if verified.

entries.title: Mortal Kombat 1
entries.definitive_edition: Mortal Kombat 1 Definitive Edition / Khaos Reigns-complete PC route

emulation.emulator: None for primary
emulation.notes: Native Windows route; no emulator required.

primary.version: Mortal Kombat 1 Definitive Edition / Khaos Reigns-complete PC route
primary.why: This is the 2023 reboot, distinct from the 1992 original. Windows has the highest fidelity/capture ceiling, while the Definitive Edition/Khaos Reigns route covers the story expansion, Kombat Pack 1, Kombat Pack 2, and associated DLC content; the Switch version had documented technical/graphics/loading issues at launch.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows version with the Definitive Edition or base game plus Definitive Edition Upgrade/Khaos Reigns content installed; verify the latest patch, cross-play state, and all DLC entitlements before capture.

entries.remaster_caveats: Do not conflate this 2023 reboot with Mortal Kombat (1992) or Mortal Kombat (2011). Khaos Reigns content is digital-only and Kombat Pack 2 is not available as a standalone character bundle.

entries.title: Mortal Kombat Armageddon

emulation.emulator: Original Xbox hardware or compatible Xbox emulator; Wii extras via Dolphin
emulation.notes: Use Xbox for the main clear, then Dolphin or real Wii hardware for the Wii-only content.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Sixth-generation console presentation for the main route; Wii extras trade online support for additional content.

primary.why: Sami selected Xbox for the main run. The PS2 and Xbox releases are the original sixth-generation versions, while the later Wii port adds exclusive extras but drops online features, so Xbox remains the main full-play route and Wii is a secondary cleanup target.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Xbox version on original hardware or a tested Xbox-emulation setup. After the main run, use the Wii version only for Khameleon and the Wii-only modes if those extras matter.

secondary.exclusive_content: Playable Khameleon, new Endurance Mode, Wii Remote Training Mode, new menu screens, and motion controls.
secondary.what_to_play: Play the Wii version only long enough to sample Khameleon and the Wii-only Endurance/Training content.
secondary.why: The Wii port adds source-backed exclusive content absent from the PS2 and Xbox versions, but it lacks online features, so it is not the main route.

entries.remaster_caveats: No modern standalone remaster exists. PS2 Premium Edition bonus material and the Wii extras do not replace the Xbox main route.

entries.title: Mortal Kombat Deadly Alliance

emulation.emulator: Original Xbox hardware or compatible Xbox emulator
emulation.notes: Use Xbox for the main route; do not substitute the reduced GBA adaptation for the full console game.

primary.why: Sami selected Xbox. It released as the same home-console family for GameCube, PS2, and Xbox; the GBA version is a constrained portable adaptation, and Tournament Edition is treated as its own archive entry.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Xbox version on original hardware or a tested Xbox-emulation setup. Use the separate Tournament Edition entry for the GBA-exclusive roster material.

entries.remaster_caveats: No modern standalone remaster exists. The GBA Tournament Edition is a related but separate portable release with different roster content.

entries.title: Mortal Kombat Deception

sami.completion_date: if glitches revert back to lower graohic version
sami.notes: psp mortal kombat uncahned esxclusive characters and gamecube shaocakn and goror

entries.definitive_edition: Mortal Kombat: Unchained is the content-complete PSP variant, but not the primary route because Sami chose Xbox.

emulation.emulator: Original Xbox hardware or compatible Xbox emulator; Dolphin for GameCube extras; PPSSPP for Unchained extras
emulation.notes: The Xbox main route should be tested if Sami's sheet warning about glitches appears; use the lower-graphics fallback only if capture/playability requires it.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Sixth-generation console main route plus portable/GC secondary extras.

primary.why: Sami selected Xbox for the main run. The Xbox and PS2 releases are the original core versions; GameCube and PSP add characters/content that are best treated as secondary cleanup because they do not replace Sami's main route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Xbox version on original hardware or a tested Xbox-emulation setup. Then use GameCube for Goro/Shao Kahn and PSP Unchained for its extra characters and Endurance Mode if pursuing every exclusive.

secondary.what_to_play: Boot the GameCube version to play the two extra characters and compare any roster-specific endings or moves of interest.
secondary.why: The GameCube version adds Goro and Shao Kahn, which are absent from the PS2/Xbox release family.

secondary.exclusive_content: Mortal Kombat: Unchained adds the GameCube characters plus Blaze, Frost, Jax, Kitana, and an exclusive Endurance Mode.
secondary.what_to_play: Use Unchained only for the extra playable characters and Endurance Mode after completing the Xbox main route.
secondary.why: The PSP version is the most content-complete variant, but it is a portable adaptation rather than Sami's chosen main route.

entries.remaster_caveats: No modern standalone remaster exists. Premium/Kollector bonus discs add extras, while GameCube and PSP add roster content.

entries.title: Mortal Kombat Onslaught

emulation.emulator: None for official play
emulation.notes: Mobile emulation cannot restore server-side/live-service availability without an official offline build or reissue.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Archival only unless an official re-release appears.

primary.why: The game only shipped on Android and iOS and was shut down on October 21, 2024, so the archive route is preservation/documentation rather than an active playable version.
primary.how_to_play: There is no current official play route. Preserve footage, account screenshots, and notes; revisit only if Warner Bros. or NetherRealm reissues the game.

entries.remaster_caveats: The live service was shut down on October 21, 2024; no offline or reissued edition exists.

emulation.emulator: Original Xbox hardware or compatible Xbox emulator
emulation.notes: Sami's note says to compare in person; if Xbox emulation has glitches, test PS2/PCSX2 as a fallback without changing the archived primary unless evidence warrants it.

primary.why: Sami selected Xbox. It released on PlayStation 2 and Xbox with no exclusive content on PS2, so Xbox remains the main route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Xbox version on original hardware or a tested Xbox-emulation setup. Use PS2 only for comparison if capture/testing shows an issue.

entries.title: Nintendo Game Boy Advance Mortal Kombat Tournament Edition Exclusive Characters

emulation.emulator: Legacy Kollection built-in emulation, or mGBA for original cartridge/ROM verification
emulation.notes: The archive target is the GBA Tournament Edition roster and modes, especially Sektor, Noob Saibot, Sareena, Survival, Tag Team, Practice, and weapon Fatalities.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Modern wrapper around the original GBA release with optional handheld display filters and convenience features.

primary.version: Mortal Kombat: Tournament Edition via Mortal Kombat: Legacy Kollection
primary.why: Tournament Edition is the GBA-only portable release that adds Sektor, Noob Saibot, and Sareena plus extra modes. With no Sami platform specified, the Windows Legacy Kollection route is the preferred primary because it preserves the handheld content in a modern wrapper with filters, aspect options, save, and rewind functionality.
primary.how_to_play: Play Mortal Kombat: Tournament Edition from Mortal Kombat: Legacy Kollection on Windows, using handheld/LCD display options as desired. Use an original GBA cartridge only if you want hardware-authentic comparison.

entries.remaster_caveats: Legacy Kollection is a preservation wrapper rather than a remake; use original GBA only for hardware-authentic comparison.

entries.title: Mortal Kombat 3
entries.definitive_edition: Mortal Kombat: Legacy Kollection PC route for access; original arcade hardware/MAME for timing verification

emulation.emulator: Legacy Kollection wrapper; MAME for arcade comparison
emulation.notes: Use the collection for normal play, original hardware/MAME for timing checks.

primary.version: Mortal Kombat: Legacy Kollection PC build, arcade Mortal Kombat 3
primary.why: Legacy Kollection is the current legal PC collection route that includes Mortal Kombat 3 and related early-series material. Because the collection has documented launch/input/online caveats, original arcade hardware or a carefully documented emulator route remains the comparison ceiling for serious timing work.
primary.how_to_play: Use Mortal Kombat: Legacy Kollection on PC and select arcade Mortal Kombat 3. Record collection patch, latency/display settings, controller/stick, online/offline state, CRT/filter/upscale settings, and whether original arcade/MAME behavior was compared.

secondary.what_to_play: Use if validating competitive or arcade-accurate feel.
secondary.why: Current collection convenience may not equal original arcade timing.

secondary.platform: SNES / Genesis / PlayStation / Saturn / PC ports
secondary.why: The arcade game is the base route.

secondary.platform: Ultimate Mortal Kombat 3 / Mortal Kombat Trilogy
secondary.what_to_play: Keep as separate entries/routes rather than replacing MK3.
secondary.why: They are related but distinct games/updates.

entries.remaster_caveats: Record collection patch and input-lag state. Do not collapse MK3, Ultimate MK3, and Mortal Kombat Trilogy into one entry.

Collection and PC ports need latency/rendering caveats.

entries.title: Ultimate Mortal Kombat 3

emulation.notes: Use official collection/cabinet when possible.

primary.version: Arcade version via current Mortal Kombat Legacy Kollection or original cabinet
primary.why: Ultimate Mortal Kombat 3 is an arcade revision/expansion of Mortal Kombat 3. The arcade version is the rules/timing target, while modern official collections are the practical access route if available; home ports vary heavily and should be labeled.
primary.how_to_play: Use the arcade version through an official collection or original cabinet/accurate arcade emulation. Record route, revision, character select, difficulty, run rules, controller/stick, display/filter/rollback state, and whether SNES/Genesis/Saturn/DS ports were compared.

entries.remaster_caveats: Record arcade revision and collection/wrapper settings.
